kept_evidence.summary: Morgan Stanley Research estimates Nvidia's Vera Rubin VR200 NVL72 rack will cost hyperscale cloud providers around $7.8 million per unit, up from roughly $4 million for the current GB300 NVL72 generation. The bank estimates Nvidia will charge about $55,000 per Rubin GPU and $5,000 per Vera CPU when sold in volume, and notes that a hyperscaler self-sourcing certain memory modules could bring the rack price down to around $6.7 million.

Morgan Stanley puts memory content per Vera Rubin VR200 rack at about $2 million, a 435% jump from the prior generation, driven by a threefold increase in LPDDR5X capacity to 54 terabytes per rack plus roughly $1 million or more in 3D NAND storage absent from earlier systems. Memory rose from 5 to 10 percent of the bill of materials on GB200 to 25 to 30 percent on VR200, while the GPU's share fell from roughly 63 percent to 51 percent.

According to Morgan Stanley's bill-of-materials analysis of Nvidia's next-generation AI rack, first shipments of the Vera Rubin VR200 NVL72 are scheduled for the third quarter of 2026, with volume ramping in the fourth quarter.

The article reports that DRAM, NAND and high-bandwidth memory supply is constrained against AI-driven demand, that contract DDR5 pricing has climbed sharply, and that device makers including Samsung and Apple are expected to pass higher memory costs into upcoming products. It adds, citing Morgan Stanley's breakdown, that memory supply tightness and lead times should be treated as a scheduling risk for AI racks comparable to accelerator allocation.
